help.title: Help
help.step.1.title: Set up the AI
help.step.1.text: Without an AI nobody can reply. The start page shows which AI is answering. Choose "Local" (runs on your graphics card, private) or "Cloud" (needs an API key from a provider).
help.step.2.title: Pick a character
help.step.2.text: Under "Characters" you find characters. Clicking the picture shows who they are; "Chat now" starts the conversation. More are in the hub, your own you create with "Create character".
help.step.3.title: Chatting
help.step.3.text: Just start writing. Text between asterisks (*smiles*) is an action. Don't like a reply? Have it rewritten – the old one stays as a variant. The character remembers your conversation.
help.step.4.title: Experience stories
help.step.4.text: In "Stage" a game master tells a story with several characters. Pick one from the gallery or create your own with the assistant. You write what your character says or does.
help.step.5.title: Voice and images
help.step.5.text: Characters can speak and create images. Set both up in the settings under "Voice" and "Images" – locally or through a service.
help.step.6.title: When something goes wrong
help.step.6.text: Error messages often offer a button with the fix. Technical fine-tuning is in the expert mode of the settings; a term is unclear? Check the glossary.
glossary.ai_model.text: The program that writes your characters' replies. Larger models usually write better but need more graphics memory or cost more in the cloud.
glossary.local_cloud.text: Local means the AI runs on your PC – private and free, but limited by your graphics card. Cloud means a provider computes for you; that needs internet and an API key.
glossary.api_key.text: A secret password from a cloud provider that lets the app fetch replies on your behalf. OtakuSoul stores it in your system's keychain.
glossary.context.text: How much of the conversation so far the AI can see at once. When it fills up, the app summarises older messages so nothing important is lost.
glossary.token.text: A piece of a word AI models count text in – roughly three to four letters. Conversation memory and cloud prices are measured in tokens.
glossary.gguf.text: The file format of local AI models. When you download a model, it is a .gguf file.
glossary.quantization.text: A shrunk version of a model. Q4 needs about half the memory of Q8 and writes only slightly worse – usually the best compromise.
glossary.vram.text: Your graphics card's memory. A local model should fit into it – the traffic light in the assistant shows whether it does.
glossary.runtime.text: The helper program that runs local models. The app downloads the right version for your graphics card by itself.
glossary.reply_style.text: How bold or precise the AI phrases things. Presets like "Creative" or "Precise" set everything up; the individual sliders (temperature …) are in expert mode.
glossary.prompt.text: The instructions the AI reads before each reply: who the character is and how to write. The app builds it from the character card.
glossary.persona.text: Who you are in the chat: your name and a short description. The characters address you that way.
glossary.lorebook.text: A reference book for a world. When a keyword comes up, the AI reads the matching entry.
glossary.macros.text: Text in double curly braces that the app fills in before each reply: {{char}} and {{user}} become the names, {{random:tea,coffee}} picks anew every time, {{pick:tea,coffee}} once per chat, {{roll:1d20}} rolls dice, {{time}}, {{date}} and {{weekday}} give the time and date, {{idle_duration}} how long you were away, {{// …}} is an invisible note.
glossary.group_chat.text: A chat with several characters. Invite more under “Group” in the chat sidebar. Whoever is addressed answers first, otherwise the AI decides who reacts. “Answer now” above the message field lets a particular character speak. Each character keeps their own memory and voice.
glossary.stage.text: Stories with several characters. A game master describes the world and side characters; your companions reply themselves.
glossary.hub.text: The online catalogue with more characters, lorebooks and stories. It shows updates as "Update available".
glossary.tts.text: Lets characters read their replies aloud – through a service or locally on your PC.
glossary.voice_clone.text: A character speaks with a voice taken from a short recording. Only allowed with the speaker's consent.
glossary.lora.text: A small add-on file for image models that teaches a style or a character. It only works with the model family it was made for.

settings.varyWordingOff: The AI writes with the normal settings. Turn on if replies often repeat themselves or start the same way.

promptSettings.post_historyHint: Optional. Sent as the last system message right before the reply, which makes it especially strong (SillyTavern's "post-history instructions").
promptSettings.postHistoryPlaceholder: e.g. Reply in at most two paragraphs.
promptSettings.previewHint: Without lorebook matches, state values and memory; in the chat those are added as they apply.
promptSettings.cardOverrides: {{name}} brings its own system prompt or post-history instructions; chats with this card use its text.

settings.gpuLayersHint: How many layers of the model run on the graphics card; the rest runs slower from main memory. Choosing a model sets a fitting value.

settings.batchHint: How much text is read in at once (batch). Larger reads long chats faster but needs more graphics memory.
settings.ubatchHint: Finer split while reading text in (ubatch). The default almost always fits.
settings.kvHint: How precisely the conversation memory is stored (KV cache). q8 (default) halves the memory with hardly any loss, allowing about twice the context; q4 saves more but is noticeably less precise. Without flash attention the V part stays f16.
settings.flashAttnHint: Faster, leaner computation (flash attention). Turn it off only if the AI crashes with this model.
settings.mlockHint: Keeps the model locked in main memory so it is not swapped out (mlock). Only useful with plenty of RAM.
settings.cpuMoeHint: Puts the experts of mixture-of-experts models into main memory (CPU MoE) – lets large models fit smaller graphics cards.
settings.reasoningModeHint: Lets thinking models reason before answering. Replies are often more thoughtful but arrive later.

settings.lorebookDepthHint: How many of the latest messages are searched for lorebook keywords. More finds more knowledge but takes room in the conversation memory.

motions.intro: Import VRM animations (.vrma, e.g. from VRoid or Booth packs) or Mixamo animations (.fbx, “Without Skin” is enough) and choose what they are for. Idle runs as a loop; gestures play on roleplay actions (*waves*, *nods*, *laughs*) and detected emotions. Without motions the built-in breathing and resting pose stays.
modelClips.title: Motions inside the model (glTF)
modelClips.intro: Animations stored in a GLB file (e.g. exported from Blender) play directly on the avatar’s own skeleton. Their use is guessed from the clip name and can be changed here; it takes precedence over imported motions with the same use. Clips set to “by hand only” are started from the gestures menu on the avatar; the mood decides which of several clips for one use is preferred.
modelClips.misfitAll: The animations in this model belong to a differently built skeleton and would distort the figure. They are not played; the figure uses the motions above instead.

storyWizard.style.fantasy: Vivid and fairy-tale-like, short paragraphs; give one clear hint per reply about what is possible next.
storyWizard.style.adventure: Dynamic and cinematic, with pace and clear choices; danger yes, cruelty no.
storyWizard.style.slice_of_life: Warm, light and lively like a slice-of-life anime; lots of dialogue, small moments.
storyWizard.style.comedy: Funny and over the top, but warm-hearted; mishaps rather than meanness.
storyWizard.style.romance: Sensitive and calm, feelings show in gestures and glances; respectful, never pushy.
storyWizard.style.mystery: Suspenseful but fair: describe clues precisely, never reveal the solution, reward good questions.
storyWizard.style.scifi: Atmospheric and believable, technology explained clearly; suspense through sounds and hints.
storyWizard.style.horror: Eerie but never cruel: shadows, sounds, hints; the ending may be touching.

storyWizard.premise.fantasy.1.opening: Lanterns of every colour float above the stalls, and it smells of honey and rain. At one stall a smiling merchant holds up a small glass orb. Inside it you see yourself as a child.

storyWizard.premise.adventure.0.location: The harbour of a small island
storyWizard.premise.adventure.0.opening: Gulls screech over the harbour as you spread the map on a barrel. A shadow falls across it. "Pretty map," says a woman in a tricorn hat. "Half of it belongs to me."
storyWizard.premise.adventure.1.title: Train Through the Storm
storyWizard.premise.adventure.1.hook: A night train across the desert, a sandstorm and a passenger who is not who he claims to be.

storyWizard.premise.adventure.1.opening: Sand rattles against the windows and the lamps in the dining car flicker. The train brakes abruptly – in the middle of nowhere. At the next table a man hastily pockets a revolver.
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.0.titl: The Little Café on the Corner
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.0.hook: You help out for a week in a tiny café – and meet the quirkiest regulars in town.
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.0.loca: A small café in a quiet side street
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.0.open: The door bell jingles and the smell of fresh pastries wraps around you. Behind the counter someone waves you over. "There you are! The coffee machine is making noises again, and the man who orders a poem every day is about to arrive."
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.1.hook: The dorm is planning a summer festival, and you accidentally ended up in charge.
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.1.loca: The courtyard of a student dorm
storyWizard.premise.slice_of_life.1.open: Fairy lights hang crookedly over the courtyard, and on the table lie stacks of flyers with your name on them – as "festival lead". Three housemates look at you expectantly. Six hours until evening.
storyWizard.premise.comedy.0.title: The Cursed Fridge
storyWizard.premise.comedy.0.hook: Your new flea-market fridge talks – and it has very strong opinions about what you should eat.
storyWizard.premise.comedy.0.opening: You open the fridge and a deep, offended voice booms: "Pudding again? I beg you." The light flickers reproachfully. Next door, someone rings the doorbell.
storyWizard.premise.comedy.1.title: A Wedding With Obstacles
storyWizard.premise.comedy.1.hook: You are the best man at your best friend's wedding – and the rings are gone.
storyWizard.premise.comedy.1.location: A castle garden on a sunny Saturday
storyWizard.premise.comedy.1.opening: The musicians tune their violins, the guests take their seats, and you pat your jacket pocket for the third time. Empty. The rose bush rustles and a magpie flies off with something glittering.
storyWizard.premise.romance.0.title: Letters Beneath the Linden Tree
storyWizard.premise.romance.0.hook: Someone leaves you anonymous letters in a hollow tree in the park – today's says: "I'll be waiting at seven."
storyWizard.premise.romance.0.location: An old linden tree in the city park
storyWizard.premise.romance.0.opening: The evening sun falls golden through the linden leaves. In the hollow lies a new envelope, sealed with a dried blossom. It is ten to seven.
storyWizard.premise.romance.1.title: Shelter in the Snowstorm
storyWizard.premise.romance.1.hook: A snowstorm forces you and a stranger to spend the night in a small mountain hut.
storyWizard.premise.romance.1.location: A mountain hut with a crackling fireplace
storyWizard.premise.romance.1.opening: Outside the storm howls, inside the fire crackles. The person who took shelter here with you silently hands you a cup of tea and smiles shyly. "Looks like we'll be here a while."
storyWizard.premise.mystery.0.title: The Secret of Room 13
storyWizard.premise.mystery.0.hook: In an old hotel a guest disappears from room 13 every night – and tonight it's yours.
storyWizard.premise.mystery.0.location: The lobby of the Grand Hotel Aurora
storyWizard.premise.mystery.0.opening: The porter hesitantly slides a brass key across the counter. The tag reads 13. "All other rooms are taken," he mumbles without looking at you. Behind you the revolving door clicks shut.
storyWizard.premise.mystery.1.title: Death of a Cake
storyWizard.premise.mystery.1.hook: At the big baking contest the winning cake was sabotaged – and everyone is pointing at you.
storyWizard.premise.mystery.1.location: The marquee of the baking contest
storyWizard.premise.mystery.1.opening: A horrified cry runs through the tent: the seven-tier winning cake has collapsed, a wooden spoon stuck right in the middle. Your name is on the handle. The jury slowly turns towards you.
storyWizard.premise.scifi.0.title: Awakening on the Ark
storyWizard.premise.scifi.0.hook: You wake from cryosleep on a generation ship – 200 years too early, and the onboard AI is silent.
storyWizard.premise.scifi.0.location: The cryo hall of the generation ship Ark
storyWizard.premise.scifi.0.opening: The pod opens with a hiss and cold mist spills out. Hundreds of other pods stand in long rows, their lights green. Only yours is red. A message blinks on the wall: YEAR 37 OF 237.
storyWizard.premise.scifi.1.title: Neon Courier
storyWizard.premise.scifi.1.hook: As a courier in a neon megacity you are to deliver a package everyone in town wants.
storyWizard.premise.scifi.1.location: A rain-soaked street in the neon district
storyWizard.premise.scifi.1.opening: Rain glitters in the hologram light and your delivery scooter hums impatiently. The package on the rack is warm – and it ticks softly. At the end of the street two black drones round the corner.
storyWizard.premise.horror.0.title: The House at the End of the Street
storyWizard.premise.horror.0.hook: You are house-sitting for your aunt for one night – and the house does not seem to want to let you go.
storyWizard.premise.horror.0.location: The hallway of an old house
storyWizard.premise.horror.0.opening: The grandfather clock in the hallway strikes midnight, although it is only ten. Upstairs a floorboard creaks, then another – as if someone were slowly pacing. Your aunt said you would be alone in the house.
storyWizard.premise.horror.1.title: The Island in the Fog
storyWizard.premise.horror.1.hook: A ferry drops you off on an island that is on no map – and does not come back.
storyWizard.premise.horror.1.location: An abandoned jetty in the fog
storyWizard.premise.horror.1.opening: The fog is so thick that after a few metres you can no longer see the ferry – only hear its horn, fainter and fainter. On the jetty stands a sign with faded letters: WELCOME BACK. Somewhere a bell is ringing.

localImage.strategy: Sharing VRAM with the chat model
localImage.strategyHint.auto: VRAM is always checked first. If the image model fits next to the chat and speech models, everything stays loaded. Otherwise the small speech model makes room first, and only if that is not enough is the chat model unloaded for the image and restarted in the background afterwards.
localImage.strategyHint.parallel: Both models stay loaded even when VRAM runs short. That can spill into system RAM and become very slow.
localImage.strategyHint.swap: The chat model is unloaded for every image and reloaded afterwards. Clean for cards below 16 GB, costs a few seconds.
localImage.strategyHint.reduce_llm: The chat model keeps only as many layers on the GPU as leave room for the image model (until the next server start). If fewer than 40 % of the layers would remain, it swaps instead.

proactive.title: Characters write on their own
proactive.intro: After a pause or when a plan is due, your characters write to you on their own – like a short message between friends.
proactive.toggle: Characters may write on their own
proactive.on: On: your characters write to you after a pause or when a plan is due.

proactive.notifyHint: A system notification when the app is not in front.
proactive.howItWorks: Characters only write while OtakuSoul is running (also in the tray), and not again before you have answered. A local AI is not started just for this. Mute single characters in the chat menu (…).

settings.chatLoraHint: A small add-on that changes how the model behaves without loading a new model. Takes effect after the next server start.

bench.title: Test the speed
bench.hint: Measures how fast the chosen model reads and writes on your PC with these settings. Usually takes 10–60 seconds; the model is loaded first if it isn't running.
bench.ratingHint.smooth: Replies appear faster than you read.
bench.ratingHint.usable: Replies appear at about reading speed. A smaller model, less context or more GPU layers make it faster.
bench.ratingHint.slow: Replies trickle in slower than you read. Pick a smaller model or put more layers on the graphics card.
bench.details: Reading: {{prompt}} tokens/s · first words after {{first}} s
proactive.dreamsHint: When you open the app after a long pause (8 hours or more), the character first tells you about a dream woven from older shared memories – once there are at least three. It also goes into their diary.
proactive.dreamImage: Send a picture of the dream
proactive.dreamImageHint: Image generation draws the dream scene that was told; the character stays recognizable from their portrait. Takes a few minutes depending on the model.
proactive.offscreenHint: In a group chat, after a long pause (8 hours or more), the character tells you instead of a dream what they did with a guest meanwhile. Both remember it.
proactive.otherChats: Also characters whose chat is not open
proactive.otherChatsHint: Characters you wrote with in the last two weeks also get in touch when their chat is not open. The message goes into their latest chat; if you are writing yourself, your reply goes first.
offscreen.memory: Spent time with {{name}} during the pause: {{text}}
micCheck.title: Audio check
micCheck.intro: Say a short sentence once. You see whether voice detection reacts, read what was understood and hear the character repeat it. It tests the settings on this page, including unsaved ones.
micCheck.thresholdMark: From here on it counts as speech
micCheck.mouth: Mouth movement for the voice output
micCheck.silent: The microphone delivers no sound. Check that the right microphone is selected and not muted.
micCheck.tooQuiet: Your voice was too quiet for the set sensitivity, so nothing was recorded.
micCheck.tooNoisy: The background noise is above the threshold, so the end of your sentence is not detected.
micCheck.noText: Speech recognition returned no text. Speak more clearly or set the language above.
micCheck.needStt: Choose a speech recognition above so the check also tests the transcript.
micCheck.needTts: Set a voice in the "Speech output" tab so the character repeats the sentence.
voiceCfg.bargeInText: During a voice call the microphone keeps listening while the character speaks. If you talk over her, she stops at once and remembers where she was interrupted. With speakers her own voice may interrupt her – use headphones or turn this off.
pet.title: Desktop pet
pet.tabTitle: Desktop pet: your character on the desktop
pet.tabIntro: The active character stands on your desktop as a 3D avatar, always on top. Mood, gestures and lip movement follow the chat.
pet.hintDrag: Press and drag to move the character. Its position is remembered.
pet.hintClick: A short click gives the character a pat.
pet.hintMenu: Right click opens the menu: mood, size, status, look at the screen and back to OtakuSoul.
pet.hintClickThrough: Next to the character, clicks go through to the windows behind it.
pet.platformNote: Made for Windows and macOS. On Linux, transparency and click-through depend on the window manager.
pet.confirmInApp: Please confirm this in the OtakuSoul window.
pet.noModel: No 3D model chosen. Pick one under “Avatars”.
pet.hintShortcut: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P or the tray icon shows and hides the pet. If it was open last, it comes back at the next start.
